title: SQL Server TRIM() Function - GeeksforGeeks
content:
The SQL Server TRIM() function omits the space character or additional stated characters from the beginning or the end of a specified string.

TRIM in SQL Server

The TRIM function in SQL Server is used to remove leading and trailing spaces from a string. It’s particularly useful for manipulating and cleaning up data, especially when performing string matching or comparisons.

To remove specific characters from a string, use the characters FROM clause.

Features of SQL TRIM function:

  • This function is used to omit the space character or some additional given characters from the beginning or the ending of a string stated.
  • This function accepts specific characters and strings.
  • This function can by default omit the front and endmost spaces from a string given.

Syntax

SQL TRIM function syntax is:

TRIM([characters FROM ]string)

Parameter:

  • characters FROM - Specific characters which are to be omitted.
  • string - Specified string from which the stated characters or spaces are omitted.

Returns:

It returns the specified string after omitting the space character or some additional stated characters from the front or the endmost part of it.

SQL Server TRIM() Function Examples

Let's look at some examples of the SQL Server TRIM() function and understand it with examples.

Example 1

Getting the specified string after omitting the beginning and ending space of it.

Query

SELECT TRIM('     GFG     ');

Output :

GFG

Example 2

Using TRIM() function with a variable and getting the specified string after modification as output.

DECLARE @str VARCHAR(10);
SET @str = '   Geeks   ';
SELECT TRIM(@str);

Output :

Geeks

Example 3

Getting the specified string after omitting the specific characters and the beginning and ending space of it.

SELECT TRIM('@$ ' FROM '    @geeksforgeeks$    ');

Output :

geeksforgeeks

Here, the specified character is also omitted.

Example 4

Using TRIM() function with two variables and getting the specified string after modification as output.

DECLARE @str VARCHAR(10);
DECLARE @char VARCHAR(10);
SET @str = '   &Geeks*  ';
SET @char = '&* ';
SELECT TRIM(@char FROM @str);

Output :

Geeks

Important Points About SQL TRIM Function

  • The SQL TRIM function is used to remove leading and/or trailing spaces or specified characters from a string.
  • By default, TRIM removes leading and trailing spaces from the input string.
  • To remove specific characters from string, use the 'characters FROM' clause.
  • TRIM returns the input string with the specified characters removed from the beginning and/or end.
  • TRIM function returns NULL if the input string is NULL.
